perspective:
Christian Mensah’s accessible information:

- He has a close childhood friendship with Jonathan; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Recently, Christian felt/observed Jonathan acting differently. He became anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important.
- He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan about it.
- He heard Jonathan admit that he had been hiding something, was in trouble, did not want to worry Christian, and had not known how to tell him.
- Christian offered help. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of a mess.
- Christian suspected the trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan directly.
- He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he himself had not done anything illegal.
- Christian decided to investigate discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up. He had some leads but did not yet know who was responsible. He told Jonathan this and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian found out who was behind it and told Jonathan it was someone they both knew and trusted. Christian felt betrayed and resolute.
- Christian planned to confront the real culprit and make sure they were brought to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous and said he trusted Christian.
- Christian’s own actions/plans include: arranging the coffee-shop meeting, confronting Jonathan, offering support, investigating discreetly, gathering evidence, clearing Jonathan’s name, confronting the culprit, and seeking justice.
